summary: Code review passed with no issues. LiveDbCollection.cs and LiveDbFixture.cs are correct xUnit shared-fixture infrastructure. CollectionDefinition with DisableParallelization=true is correctly applied. LiveDbFixture correctly implements IDisposable (no-op), exposes the required public API (SkipReason, Csb, CreateConnection), encapsulates all four config-resolution methods and the TestConnectionConfig record as private members, and enforces the spdb_tests schema guard. comments.note: No blocking issues found. Both files are clean and correct. The xUnit IClassFixture + CollectionDefinition pattern is implemented correctly. The spdb_tests schema-name guard in BuildConnectionString is appropriately defensive. The two-source config resolution (env var → file walk) is a sound CI/CD pattern. ParseConfigFile uses GetProperty() (throws on missing keys) for required fields and TryGetProperty for optional fields — this is intentional: malformed config should fail loudly. The Dispose() no-op is correct and documented.

Organizational inconsistency: LiveDbCollection.cs and LiveDbFixture.cs are placed at the project root (namespace VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.Tests) while the existing Fixtures/ subfolder (Fixtures/TempDirectory.cs) uses namespace VideoIndexer.Infrastructure.Tests.Fixtures. Since the migration WP (adding [Collection("LiveDB")] to test classes) hasn't run yet, there are no consumers — moving to Fixtures/ would be cost-free now but adds a namespace import to the migration WP. The team should decide the convention before the migration WP executes.

[documentation-forward] Tests README (or test infrastructure guide) should document: (1) how to use LiveDbFixture in a test class (add IClassFixture<LiveDbFixture>, [Collection("LiveDB")], and call Skip.If(fixture.SkipReason is not null, fixture.SkipReason)), (2) the two config sources (test-config.json and VI_TEST_CONNECTION env var), and (3) that the shared spdb_tests schema is the mandatory target enforced by the fixture. This will help contributors set up their local environment correctly.
